newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas in talks with Aussie over facilities.
newsitem.headline: Qantas in talks with Aussie over facilities.

text.p: Australian government-owned Federal Airports Corp (FAC) said on Thursday Qantas Airways Ltd was still in talks with airline hopeful Aussie Airlines over Qantas sub-leasing some facilities to Aussie for a period of time.
"Discussions are continuing and I will be pressing both parties to formalise an agreement," Murphy told reporters after speaking the American Chamber of Commerce in Australia.
"If they can't achieve that, well that's okay, that's life in the commercial world," Murphy said.
Murphy said he would meet Aussie Airlines owner Bryan Grey on Friday. Grey was the former head of the first Compass Airlines, which failed in 1991.

The talks centre around Qantas, Australia's largest airline, sub-leasing facilities at five airports around Australia, so that Aussie Airlines could compete with Qantas and fellow domestic operator Ansett Airlines Ltd.
Local media reports that Grey is still in talks with financiers about the development of a domestic airline.
